about: The state paths the SHELL reads and the JSON kind each answers (docs/lanes/realcore-firstrun.testplan.md P1, P3). Generated rows come from `python3 checks/parity-paths.py --write`; the hand-typed fields are kept. NOTATION: a path is `<name>` where an id goes (`label/<label>/chains/<placement>`); `instances` lists the values, else the test takes them from the real core (label, provider, agent, message, thread); any other placeholder needs `instances`. The checker also reads `*` as a wildcard and a concrete id (`ai_provider/jev/state`) as covered by a typed `<provider>` row, so a read is never reported twice. KIND is a JSON kind (`object`, `array`, `string`, `bool`, `number`, `null`, joined by `|`) or `absent` (the core never answers). UNTYPED: a row whose `kind` is null is a path the shell reads and nobody typed. It is a FINDING, not a default: `--write` adds such rows so the gap is visible the moment a read is created; `parity-paths.py` ends `N untyped` and exits 1 on N > 0; state_parity.rs prints `UNTYPED <path>: add its kind` and fails in words (never a panic). To type one, read what the real core answers (engine rust_core.rs `state`) and write the kind; where the real core does not serve it, write `gap`; where it answers only sometimes, `empty_by_design` with the reason. `empty_by_design` may answer nothing, and says why. `gap` is a path the fixture serves and the real core does not: the test requires it to stay unanswered and prints it, so a path that becomes served is moved out of the gaps. `rig_only` (a reason) is a path only a rig core serves (tests, never the owner's copy): state_parity skips it on its new-installation core and prints it; the fixture is not required to serve it.
not_covered: inbox and message paths (message/<id>/starred, archived, snoozed, muted), draft/<id>/*, outbox/<id>/*, mcp_*, split_tab/*, smart_folder/*, search/recent, notch, relay and system ports, import/<run>/*, thread/<id>/reminder: other panes, for the generated file
